category: Toolbar tools I - selection, crop, slice and measure
description: The upper half of the Photoshop toolbar: the move and artboard tools, the marquee/lasso/object-selection family, crop and slice tools, the frame tool, and the sampling and measurement tools. Tools that share a slot cycle with Shift plus the slot's letter.

tools.name: Move Tool
tools.description: Moves the contents of the active layer, a selection, guides or a whole layer group. With Auto-Select on it picks the layer or group under the pointer; with Show Transform Controls on it exposes free-transform handles without invoking Edit > Free Transform. The options bar also holds the align and distribute buttons used when several layers are selected.
tools.usage: Toolbar (V). Hold Ctrl to switch to it temporarily from most painting tools.

parameters.name: Auto-Select
parameters.description: Layer or Group - clicking picks the topmost layer/group with pixels under the cursor instead of moving the active layer.

parameters.name: Show Transform Controls
parameters.description: Draws scale/rotate handles around the layer bounds.

parameters.name: Align / Distribute
parameters.description: Align edges and centres, and distribute spacing, across the selected layers.

tools.example:
1. Press V and click a shape on the canvas.
2. Hold Alt and drag to duplicate the layer as you move it.
3. Nudge by 1 px with the arrow keys, or 10 px with Shift+arrow.

JSX equivalent:
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.translate(50, -20);
tools.notes: Alt+drag duplicates; Shift constrains movement to 45 degree increments. Nothing moves if the layer is locked or the pixels lie outside the current selection.

tools.name: Artboard Tool
tools.description: Creates and manages artboards - named, independently sized canvases inside one document, used for responsive UI designs, social-media size sets and multi-page layouts. Dragging on empty canvas makes a new artboard; the plus buttons beside an existing artboard clone it in that direction. Each artboard exports as its own file with Export As.
tools.usage: Toolbar (V, shares the slot with the Move tool; press Shift+V to cycle).

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: Preset device/paper sizes (iPhone, Web, A4, ...) or a custom width and height.

parameters.name: Add artboard buttons
parameters.description: The + handles around a selected artboard add a duplicate to the left, right, above or below.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+V to select the Artboard tool.
2. Pick "iPhone 14 Pro" from the Size menu in the options bar.
3. Click the + handle on the right edge to add a second artboard of the same size.
4. File > Export > Export As, tick "Export all artboards".

tools.name: Rectangular Marquee Tool
tools.description: Draws rectangular pixel selections. The simplest selection tool, used for cropping regions, filling boxes, constraining filters to an area and creating rectangular masks. The options bar controls the boolean mode (new, add, subtract, intersect), feathering and a fixed ratio or fixed size.
tools.usage: Toolbar (M). Shift+M cycles to the Elliptical Marquee.

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Normal, Fixed Ratio (e.g. 16:9) or Fixed Size (exact pixel dimensions).

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.description: Softens the selection edge by the given radius before the selection is made.

parameters.name: Boolean mode
parameters.description: Hold Shift to add to the selection, Alt to subtract, Shift+Alt to intersect.

tools.notes: Drag from the centre by holding Alt. Selection edges are anti-aliased only for the elliptical and lasso tools; rectangular selections are always hard-edged unless feathered.

tools.name: Elliptical Marquee Tool
tools.description: Draws elliptical and circular pixel selections, with the same boolean, feather and style options as the rectangular marquee plus an Anti-alias checkbox. Used for vignettes, round crops, circular masks and selecting eyes or lenses during retouching.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+M to cycle from the Rectangular Marquee).

parameters.name: Anti-alias
parameters.description: Smooths the jagged stair-stepping on the curved edge. Leave it on for almost all work.

parameters.name: Style
parameters.description: Normal, Fixed Ratio or Fixed Size.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+M until the Elliptical Marquee is active.
2. Hold Shift+Alt and drag from the centre of an eye to select a perfect circle around it.
3. Select > Modify > Feather (10 px), then add a Curves adjustment layer - the selection becomes its mask.

tools.name: Single Row / Single Column Marquee Tool
tools.description: Selects a one-pixel-tall row or one-pixel-wide column across the whole canvas. Mostly used to build hairline rules, to sample and stretch a single scanline into a gradient or streak effect, and to check a single line of pixels for banding.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+M cycles through the four marquee tools).
tools.example:
1. Choose the Single Column Marquee and click anywhere in the image.
2. Ctrl+J to copy the column to its own layer.
3. Ctrl+T and scale it horizontally across the canvas to create a streak/smear background.
tools.notes: These two tools have no keyboard letter of their own; reach them by cycling with Shift+M or from the toolbar fly-out.

tools.name: Lasso Tool
tools.description: Draws a freehand selection that closes automatically when you release the mouse. The fastest way to rough in an area for a local adjustment, a Content-Aware Fill or the Remove tool, where exact edges do not matter.
tools.usage: Toolbar (L). Shift+L cycles to the Polygonal and Magnetic Lasso.

parameters.name: Feather
parameters.description: Edge softness in pixels applied as the selection is created.

parameters.name: Anti-alias
parameters.description: Smooths the selection edge.

tools.example:
1. Press L and draw loosely around a blemish.
2. Shift+F5 (Edit > Fill) > Content-Aware > OK.
3. Ctrl+D to deselect.
tools.notes: Hold Alt while using the Lasso to temporarily switch to straight-line (Polygonal) segments.

tools.name: Polygonal Lasso Tool
tools.description: Builds a selection from straight-line segments: each click sets a corner, double-clicking or clicking the start point closes the path. Ideal for buildings, boxes, screens and any subject bounded by straight edges.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+L to cycle from the Lasso).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+L until the Polygonal Lasso is active.
2. Click each corner of a window frame; press Backspace to undo the last point.
3. Double-click to close the selection.
tools.notes: Hold Shift to constrain a segment to 45 degree increments; hold Alt and drag to draw a freehand segment mid-polygon.

tools.name: Magnetic Lasso Tool
tools.description: Snaps the selection edge to the strongest contrast boundary near the cursor as you trace, dropping anchor points automatically. Works well on high-contrast subjects against a plain background and poorly on soft or busy edges.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+L to cycle).

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Detection radius in pixels around the cursor that is searched for an edge.

parameters.name: Contrast
parameters.description: How much edge contrast (%) is required before the tool snaps.

parameters.name: Frequency
parameters.description: How often anchor points are laid down (higher = more points, tighter tracking).

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+L until the Magnetic Lasso is active; set Width 10 px, Contrast 10%, Frequency 57.
2. Click once on the subject edge and trace around it; click to force an anchor point where it drifts.
3. Press Backspace to remove the last anchor, Enter to close the selection.
tools.notes: For most cut-outs the Object Selection tool followed by Select and Mask now gives a better result with far less work.

tools.name: Object Selection Tool
tools.description: Adobe Sensei-powered selection: draw a rectangle or lasso around an object, or simply hover and click a highlighted object, and Photoshop selects just that object. Object Finder mode pre-computes every object in the image so you can select them by hovering. The fastest route to a usable subject selection before refining it in Select and Mask.
tools.usage: Toolbar (W). Shift+W cycles to Quick Selection and Magic Wand.

parameters.name: Object Finder
parameters.description: Pre-analyses the image and highlights each detected object under the cursor for one-click selection.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Rectangle or Lasso for the region you draw around the object.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Analyse the composite image rather than only the active layer.

tools.example:
1. Press W, enable Object Finder in the options bar and wait for the analysis to finish.
2. Hover the subject until it highlights, then click to select it.
3. Shift-click a second object to add it; Alt-click to subtract.
4. Click Select and Mask... to refine hair and edges.

tools.name: Quick Selection Tool
tools.description: A brush that grows a selection outwards as you paint, following texture, colour and tone boundaries. Good for medium-contrast subjects and for quickly extending an Object Selection result. Bracket keys resize the brush while you work.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+W to cycle).

parameters.name: Brush size
parameters.description: Set with [ and ]; larger brushes make bolder, less precise grabs.

parameters.name: Enhance Edge
parameters.description: Pulls the selection boundary towards image edges and smooths it.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Bases the selection on the composite of all visible layers.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+W to reach Quick Selection.
2. Paint over the subject; hold Alt and paint to push the selection back out of over-selected areas.
3. Press Q to preview the result as a Quick Mask overlay.

tools.name: Magic Wand Tool
tools.description: Selects contiguous (or, with Contiguous off, all) pixels whose colour is within a tolerance of the clicked pixel. Still the quickest way to select a flat sky, a solid backdrop or a single colour in a logo or screenshot.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+W to cycle).

parameters.name: Tolerance
parameters.description: 0-255 colour distance from the sampled pixel. 32 is the default; raise it for gradients.

parameters.name: Contiguous
parameters.description: On: only the connected region. Off: every matching pixel in the layer.

parameters.name: Sample Size
parameters.description: Point sample or an averaged 3x3 - 101x101 area, shared with the Eyedropper.

parameters.name: Sample All Layers
parameters.description: Evaluate the composite rather than the active layer.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+W until the Magic Wand is active; set Tolerance 24, Contiguous on.
2. Click the white background of a product shot.
3. Shift+Ctrl+I to invert the selection onto the product, then add a layer mask.
tools.notes: Select > Grow and Select > Similar extend a wand selection using the same tolerance value.

tools.name: Crop Tool
tools.description: Trims and straightens the canvas. Drag the handles or enter a ratio/resolution in the options bar; with Delete Cropped Pixels off the crop is non-destructive and the trimmed area can be recovered later. The Straighten button lets you draw a line along a horizon to level the image, and Content-Aware fills the corners left empty by a rotation.
tools.usage: Toolbar (C). Press Enter to commit, Esc to cancel.

parameters.name: Ratio / W x H x Resolution
parameters.description: Free crop, a preset or a custom aspect ratio; the second mode also resamples to a target pixel size and resolution.

parameters.name: Straighten
parameters.description: Draw a line along something that should be horizontal or vertical to auto-rotate.

parameters.name: Delete Cropped Pixels
parameters.description: Off keeps the cropped data inside the document so the crop stays editable.

parameters.name: Content-Aware
parameters.description: Generatively fills areas outside the original image after a rotation or an expanded crop.

tools.example:
1. Press C, choose 16:9 from the ratio menu.
2. Untick Delete Cropped Pixels so the crop remains reversible.
3. Drag to frame, then press Enter.

JSX equivalent:
app.activeDocument.crop([100, 50, 1900, 1100], 0, UnitValue(1800,'px'), UnitValue(1050,'px'));

tools.name: Perspective Crop Tool
tools.description: Crops and corrects perspective distortion in one step: drag a quadrilateral over a skewed rectangular subject (a document, a painting, a building facade) and Photoshop maps it back to a true rectangle. Useful for flattening photographed pages and de-keystoning architecture.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+C to cycle from the Crop tool).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+C to select the Perspective Crop tool.
2. Click the four corners of a photographed whiteboard in order.
3. Drag the corner handles to fine-tune, then press Enter to flatten the perspective.

tools.name: Slice Tool
tools.description: Divides an image into rectangular slices that are exported as separate files (with optional HTML table or CSS) by File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy). A legacy web-production workflow, largely replaced by artboards and Export As, but still used for sprite sheets and email templates.
tools.usage: Toolbar (C; press Shift+C to cycle to it).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+C until the Slice tool is active and drag boxes over each button in a mockup.
2. Switch to the Slice Select tool, double-click a slice and give it a name and link.
3. File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy), set "Slices: All User Slices" and save.

tools.name: Slice Select Tool
tools.description: Selects, moves, resizes, divides, stacks and deletes existing slices, and opens the Slice Options dialog where a slice's name, URL, alt text and background are set. Also promotes auto-slices (generated by Photoshop) to user slices.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+C to cycle).
tools.example:
1. Choose the Slice Select tool and click a slice.
2. Click "Divide..." in the options bar to split it into 3 equal columns.
3. Double-click the slice to set its Name and URL in Slice Options.

tools.name: Frame Tool
tools.description: Draws a rectangular or elliptical placeholder frame that automatically masks whatever image you drop into it, scaling the content to fill. Frames make image placeholders in layout work behave like InDesign frames: replace the content by dragging a new file onto the frame without touching the mask.
tools.usage: Toolbar (K). Options bar switches between rectangular and elliptical frames.
tools.example:
1. Press K and drag a rectangle where the photo should go.
2. Drag an image file from Explorer (or a Library asset) onto the frame - it is placed as a smart object and clipped.
3. Click the content thumbnail in the Layers panel and press Ctrl+T to scale the image inside the frame.
tools.notes: Convert any shape or text layer into a frame with Layer > New > Convert to Frame.

tools.name: Eyedropper Tool
tools.description: Samples a colour from the image into the foreground swatch (Alt-click for the background swatch). The Sample Size menu averages over an area, which avoids picking up noise, and Sample can read the current layer, the layer below or all layers, with or without adjustment layers applied.
tools.usage: Toolbar (I). Hold Alt with a painting tool active to sample temporarily.

parameters.name: Sample Size
parameters.description: Point Sample, or 3x3, 5x5, 11x11, 31x31, 51x51, 101x101 Average.

parameters.name: Sample
parameters.description: All Layers, Current Layer, Current & Below, with or without adjustments.

parameters.name: Show Sampling Ring
parameters.description: Displays a ring showing the new colour against the previous one while dragging.

tools.example:
1. Press I, set Sample Size to 5 by 5 Average.
2. Click a midtone in the skin to load it as the foreground colour.
3. Alt+click a highlight to load it as the background colour.
tools.notes: Dragging outside the Photoshop window while sampling picks colours from anywhere on screen.

tools.name: Color Sampler Tool
tools.description: Places up to ten persistent sample points whose RGB/CMYK/Lab values are shown live in the Info panel. Essential for colour correction: park samplers on a known neutral, a highlight and a shadow and watch the numbers while you drag Curves.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+I to cycle from the Eyedropper).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+I to get the Color Sampler and click on a patch that should be neutral grey.
2. Open the Info panel (F8) and add a Curves adjustment layer.
3. Adjust the individual R, G and B curves until sampler #1 reads roughly equal values.
tools.notes: Alt+click a sampler to delete it; Clear All in the options bar removes them all. Samplers are saved with the document.

tools.name: Ruler Tool
tools.description: Measures distance, angle and delta between two points, reporting them in the options bar and Info panel. Its Straighten Layer button rotates the layer so the measured line becomes horizontal or vertical, which is the standard way to level a horizon precisely.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+I to cycle).
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+I until the Ruler tool is active.
2. Drag along a horizon line that should be level.
3. Click "Straighten Layer" in the options bar.
tools.notes: Hold Alt and drag from one end of an existing measure line to create a protractor and read an angle between two lines.

tools.name: Note Tool
tools.description: Attaches a text annotation to a point in the document. Notes are stored in the PSD/PDF and are visible to anyone who opens the file, which makes them a simple way to pass review feedback or production instructions along with the artwork.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+I to cycle). Notes are read and edited in Window > Notes.
tools.example:
1. Press Shift+I until the Note tool is active and click on the area in question.
2. Type "Client wants this logo 10% larger" in the Notes panel.
3. Save as PSD or PDF - the note travels with the file.
tools.notes: Notes are not exported into flattened JPEG/PNG output. Shared Document review comments (Window > Comments) are the cloud alternative.

tools.name: Count Tool
tools.description: Numbers objects as you click them and keeps a running total in the options bar, with multiple named count groups in different colours. Used in scientific, medical and inventory imaging; it can also auto-count the elements inside a selection.
tools.usage: Toolbar (Shift+I to cycle). Analysis data appears in Window > Measurement Log.

parameters.name: Count Group
parameters.description: Named groups, each with its own colour, marker size and label size.

parameters.name: Clear
parameters.description: Resets the current group's count to zero.

tools.example:
1. Press Shift+I until the Count tool is active.
2. Click each cell in a microscope image; the count increments in the options bar.
3. Make a selection and choose Image > Analysis > Record Measurements to log the counted items.

tools.name: Hand, Zoom and screen navigation (toolbar footer)
tools.description: The bottom of the toolbar holds the foreground/background colour swatches (D resets to black/white, X swaps them), the Quick Mask toggle (Q) and the screen-mode cycle (F). These are shared by every tool and are the fastest way to set painting colours, to preview a selection as a red overlay and to switch to a distraction-free full-screen canvas.
tools.usage: Toolbar footer. D = default colours, X = swap, Q = Quick Mask, F = cycle screen modes, Tab = hide all panels.
tools.example:
1. Make a rough selection, press Q to enter Quick Mask.
2. Press D then paint with black to remove areas from the selection and white to add them.
3. Press Q again to return to a refined selection.
tools.notes: Shift+Tab hides the side panels but keeps the options bar and toolbar visible.
